# `razor_attribute_indent_style`

With curb_razor_format_markup, where an attribute that starts a line inside a start tag goes. Microsoft's Razor formatter reads the same key.

## Values

| Value | Notes |
|---|---|
| `align_with_first` | |
| `indent_by_one` | |
| `indent_by_two` | |

**Default:** `align_with_first`

Microsoft's Razor formatter reads the same key with the same values, so one setting serves both. It only applies with `curb_razor_format_markup`. A line inside a start tag that begins with its `>` or `/>` goes where the tag's line does, C# continuing an attribute's value moves as far as the tag's line moved, and text continuing a quoted value is kept as written, since its whitespace is part of the value. With nothing after the tag's name on its line, `align_with_first` puts attributes a level in; Microsoft's formatter, and `curb_razor_markup_engine_quirks`, align them with the tag instead. The examples here are at `indent_size = 2`.

### `razor_attribute_indent_style = align_with_first`

```ini
razor_attribute_indent_style = align_with_first
```

::::{tab-set}

:::{tab-item} Before
```html
<div>
<button class="btn btn-primary" type="button"
@onclick="Save"
disabled="@busy">
Save
</button>
<InputText
@bind-Value="name"
placeholder="Name" />
</div>
```
:::

:::{tab-item} After
```html
<div>
  <button class="btn btn-primary" type="button"
          @onclick="Save"
          disabled="@busy">
    Save
  </button>
  <InputText
    @bind-Value="name"
    placeholder="Name" />
</div>
```
:::

::::
